urls.note: PRIMARY. The whole payment-recourse finding rests on s.75 and the s.75(3)(b) cash-price thresholds. Nothing about UK card recourse gets published until this section is read verbatim.
Source of the 'it is the cash price, not what you put on the card' wording — the part that makes a deposit on a made-to-order doll covered. Quoted only from a search snippet so far.
Statutory body. Wanted for the deposit / part-payment worked example, which is the exact shape of a doll pre-order.

Checks the claim that s.75 thresholds are unchanged and connected-lender reform was deferred. If wrong, the finding is time-expired rather than false. [run 1: the phase-2 publication URL 404d; switched to the collection page]
Second, independent read on the state of CCA reform.

s.170 CEMA 1979, cited as the route by which UK legal risk in this category runs through import rather than possession. Relevant to what we tell readers about importing; must not be paraphrased unread.

CPS guidance. Needed to state UK legal exposure accurately, and specifically to check whether any height or appearance 'safe harbour' test for adult-form dolls exists. The research found NO such threshold — vendor and forum claims of the form 'over X cm is legal' are unconfirmed and must not be repeated.

Phthalates measured in sex toys above CPSC children's-toy limits, and the absence of any risk-assessment regime for the category. Would be a materially stronger finding than anything published; killed only for lack of retrieval.

HPV DNA persisting on a toy surface after cleaning with a commercial cleaner, and the authors' statement that no evidence-based cleaning protocol exists. Bears directly on our care-and-cleaning page, which currently gives advice this may undercut.

The most-cited empirical dataset on who owns these products. Wanted to check (a) what it actually found and (b) whether the widely-repeated '~37% report guilt or shame' figure appears in it at all — the research could not find it in the thesis, only in later work citing it.
